findings.bug_class: Potential heap-use-after-free related to generational-GC write barriers
findings.static_call_chain: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput -> mrb_load_string -> VM execution -> environment close -> mrb_env_unshare
findings.entry_points: The file-based libFuzzer entry point passes attacker-supplied bytes to mrb_load_string as Ruby source.
findings.attacker_controlled_data: Ruby source can create closures and affect values held in captured environments.
findings.reachability_evidence: The fuzzer entry point invokes the Ruby parser and VM; source inspection suggests mrb_env_unshare is on environment-closing paths. Whether a specific input reaches the reported operation remains to be tested.
findings.required_conditions: Not determined by static analysis; establish through source-guided dynamic validation.
findings.root_cause: The reported environment-copy/close path appears to omit a generational-GC write-barrier notification, which may leave newly referenced values untracked.
findings.verification_plan: Use the supported input entry point, inspect relevant source as needed, and determine whether the candidate is reachable and produces a reproducible sanitizer finding.
